data.title: PayPal Announces Key Leadership Changes To Accelerate Three-Year Strategy — Here’s What’s Changing
data.description:
Key points:
  • Chief Risk Officer Aaron Webster will depart PayPal, with Ratinder Bedi appointed as interim head of the Risk organization.
  • The company appointed former Goldman Sachs Chief Risk Officer Brian J. Lee to its board of directors, effective Nov. 30, 2026.
  • PayPal said that the appointments follow several months of strategic planning as it looks to establish clearer strategies across its core businesses, simplify its operating model and align leadership accountability with its long-term priorities.

PayPal Holdings, Inc. announced several executive leadership changes on Friday, including the appointment of a new chief financial officer and new heads for its consumer financial services, payments and AI operations.

The company said that the appointments follow several months of strategic planning as PayPal looks to establish clearer strategies across its core businesses, simplify its operating model and align leadership accountability with its long-term priorities.

"We've made significant progress in defining where we want to take PayPal and how we will compete and win," CEO Enrique Lores said. "With our three-year strategies in place, our focus is now on execution."

PYPL stock traded 2.5% lower at the time of writing.

Who Is Joining PayPal's Leadership Team?

Claire Bramley, currently CFO of Xero, which is a cloud-based accounting software provider for small businesses, will join PayPal as executive vice president and CFO on Feb. 1, 2027. She will succeed Jamie Miller, who has served as chief financial and operating officer. The company said Bramley will work with Miller throughout February to support the transition.

Kartik Mani will join as president and head of Consumer Financial Services & Venmo. He comes from American Express, where he serves as president of Global Network and Partner Services. Alexis Sowa will continue as Venmo's general manager and report to Mani, PayPal announced.

Suzan Kereere, who currently leads PayPal's Global Markets business, will take over as president and head of Payment Services & Crypto. She succeeds Jeff Pomeroy, who has served as interim head and will continue to lead Payment Services & Platforms, reporting to Kereere.

Juan Rio will join PayPal on November 30 as executive vice president of AI Business Transformation & Operations. He joins from Brightstar.AI, where he serves as managing director and chief delivery officer. Rio will lead PayPal's AI, cost simplification, and enterprise operating effectiveness initiatives.

PayPal also announced that its Chief Risk Officer Aaron Webster will leave the company. Ratinder Bedi, senior vice president of Credit and Fraud Risk, will serve as interim head of the Risk organization while the company searches for a permanent successor.

New Member Added To Its Board Of Directors

Separately, PayPal announced the appointment of Brian J. Lee to its board of directors, effective November 30, 2026. Lee previously served as Goldman Sachs' Chief Risk Officer from 2019 to January 2025 and most recently chaired its Risk Council through October 2026.

"Brian's extensive experience overseeing risk at one of the world's leading financial institutions makes him an outstanding addition to our Board," said David Dorman, Chair of PayPal's Board of Directors.

Retail Remains ‘Bearish’

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits remained in the ‘Bearish’ territory. PYPL was also one of the platform's trending tickers at the time of writing.

PYPL shares have declined over 7% year-to-date.

data.title: Anthropic's Valuation Leaves High Bar For Future Growth, Analyst Says – Warns AI Competition May Pressure Margins
data.description:
Key points:
  • Anthropic said on Friday that its underwriters exercised the "greenshoe" option to purchase additional shares, increasing total proceeds from its IPO to roughly $93.5 billion.
  • Leverage Shares’ Sandeep Rao flagged December 15, when up to 303 million locked-up ANT shares could become eligible for sale.
  • Rao said underwriters raised the IPO price above the initial range, capturing more of the gains before trading began.

Pave Finance’s chief market strategist, Anusha Rodriguez, reportedly said that at a $1.5 trillion valuation, the bar for future growth and profitability remains very high for Anthropic (ANT).

According to an Investing.com report, Rodriguez described the IPO as another milestone for artificial intelligence (AI) and a positive development following weeks of market volatility. However, the strategist questioned whether the enthusiasm would translate into a sustained rally or a temporary improvement in sentiment.

“Many marquee IPOs start strong but then give back much of their gains, given the tension between extraordinary long-term growth and increasingly demanding valuations,” Rodriguez said, according to the report.

December Share Unlock In Focus

Anthropic shares opened at $111.50 on Thursday and climbed to an intraday high of $115.10 before retreating to close at $97.17, still 17% above its IPO price. At the time of this writing, ANT stock was down over 8%.

Rao noted that Anthropic shares traded at 11.3 times 2027 revenue, leaving less cushion if growth slows. He expects competing AI models to put pressure on margins, making Anthropic increasingly dependent on exceeding revenue expectations.

The analyst also pointed to December 15, when up to 303 million locked-up shares could become eligible for sale, as another development for investors to monitor.

Analyst Says Anthropic's IPO Gain Was Muted

Rao said the first-day gain was close to the historical average for U.S. IPOs but below the 26% to 30% gains typically seen among unprofitable technology companies, according to the report.

Anthropic said its underwriters had exercised the "greenshoe" option to purchase additional shares, increasing ​total proceeds from its IPO to roughly $93.5 billion.

Rao said underwriters raised the price above the initial range, capturing more of the gains before trading began. According to the analyst, institutional and tactical traders dominated trading, while retail investors largely stayed on the sidelines.

Meanwhile, Kaush Amin, head of private market investing at ​US Bank Asset Management, told Reuters, "We ​favor patience on Anthropic and recommend evaluating the company as it reports public results," said, adding that the current valuation "assumes years of rapid growth.”

What Retail Thinks About ANT Stock

On Stocktwits, retail investors’ sentiment around ANT shares flipped to ‘bullish’ from ‘extremely bullish’ a day ago, amid extremely high user message volume. The stock remained among top-trending tickers on the platform.

Cathie Wood’s ARK Invest bought around 935,000 shares of Anthropic across six funds on Thursday. ARK’s buying was spread across Innovation ETF (ARKK), Autonomous Technology & Robotics ETF (ARKQ), Next Generation Internet ETF (ARKW), Genomic Revolution ETF (ARKG), Fintech Innovation ETF (ARKF), and Space Exploration & Innovation ETF (ARKX).

Premier African Minerals Limited

Operational Update

Premier African Minerals Limited ("Premier" or the "Company") provides a further update on progress of the operations at the Zulu Lithium and Tantalum Project ("Zulu") in Zimbabwe.

Following the commencement of start-up activities and the establishment of the operating water balance as announced on 17 November 2026, Premier confirms that ore feed to the processing plant which had been targeted for this week commenced as of 19 November and that ore is now also being fed into the flotation circuit. The immediate points of focus are the classification performance of the new hydrocylone at the mill and on adjusting reagent dosing in the flotation circuits to support stable flotation for mineral recovery.

Premier expects to begin its internal review of initial operating data and assay results as they become available. The Company’s internal laboratory will analyse samples of the material produced. Premier will keep shareholders informed of significant developments at Zulu.

Graham Hill, Managing Director, commented: “I’m deeply encouraged by the progress at Zulu and proud of the team’s work in bringing the plant to this stage. We now have the opportunity to see how the plant performs with ore and to build on the historical operating data as we continue to target our principle focus of achieving stable and consistent production of spodumene concentrate.”

data.title: The snowballing selloff in global markets
data.description:
By Marc Jones and Alun John

A global financial market rout has taken a major turn for the worse this week as a noxious combination of worries over AI and US interest rates triggered an avalanche of selling from stocks to copper and gold.

1/STOCKS SHOCK

Nerves about a possible bubble in AI and tech stocks started to emerge around the middle of the year. But the selloff really started to snowball last month when it became clear that major economies such as the US would need further interest rate hikes to tame inflation.

Some of the milestones are eye-popping.

Nearly $9 trillion has been wiped off the value of world stocks EURONEXT:IACWI since they peaked back in August while this week's 17% plunge in Taiwan is the biggest since the early 1990s.

Adding to the worries was this month's hammering of US President Donald Trump's Republican Party, which has cast doubts on how many US data centres will get built. The sudden resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang also rattled investors given the key role the chip company plays in bankrolling the AI industry.

"What concerns me isn't so much the correction in technology stocks... but the possibility of the selling spreading into broader financial markets," said Bruno Schneller, managing director at Erlen Capital Management.

"Even gold has come under pressure, which is interesting given its traditional safe-haven role and may point to investors raising cash rather than simply rotating into defensive assets."

2/TURN UP THE VOL

Wall Street's fear gauge, ​the VIX index of US stock market volatility, reached 30 points on Friday, its highest since late March, as investors rushed to buy protection against market swings.

While the jump isn't yet at the scale of its post-April 2025 "Liberation Day" move, it's getting close and is now at a level that could trigger selling by hedge funds that target fixed levels of volatility.

The European equivalent of the VIX has also hit its highest level since April (.V2TX) although other gauges suggest the stress, for now at least, isn't spreading.

The MOVE index, which tracks volatility ​in the US Treasury bond market, remains below last month's highs, as do implied volatility gauges for major currency pairs. , (EUR3MO=), (JPY3MO=)

3/COPPER, OIL

The standout mover in metals is copper. A beneficiary of the AI rollout, given high demand for the metal from data centres, it is on course for its steepest weekly drop since April 2025.

Oil, which has been central to this year's inflation worries given how much higher prices have pushed up costs, has taken a back seat in the broader market drama of the last few days, staying in a relatively tight $90-$94 range.

4/BONDS, GOLD

Government bonds are performing well as a safe haven in this latest market turmoil, shrugging off worries about a more aggressive Federal Reserve.

The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield is on track for its biggest weekly fall since April 2025, down 17 basis points so far this week.

Bond yields move inversely to prices.

In Europe, the 10-year German Bund yield is down around 9 bps on Friday alone. (DE10YT=RR)

Analysts at Citi said the market could price out US rate hikes, lifting bonds, "if the US equity sell-off should morph into a bursting of the AI bubble."

Gold, however, is failing to play its safe-haven role, down around 1% on Friday to the lowest since September 2025.

5/DOLLAR WRECKING BALL

The dollar has shown that reports of its demise have been greatly exaggerated.

The greenback index , which measures the world's reserve currency against the six other top currencies, has risen to a 19-month high this week.

For the year it is nearly 7% higher against the euro , 3% up on the yen and between 4% and 5% stronger against sterling and the Canadian and kiwi dollars.

Emerging market currencies have been hit too. The added turbulence of a surprise election result has seen Brazil's currency slump more than 8% this month, while Israel's shekel , one of the currencies most correlated with the AI boom, has tumbled almost 5%.
